reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Strong evidence - epidural placement was successfully achieved with documented drug delivery (0.1% ropivacaine + 10 mcg/mL hydromorphone at 6 mL/hr). This confirms the drugs reached their intended target (spinal nociceptive pathways). 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: Good evidence - IL-2 levels were lower in the epidural group (9.6 vs 15.5 nmol/L), suggesting reduced inflammatory response consistent with effective pain pathway blockade. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Clear success - primary endpoint was met with a clinically meaningful effect size of -1.08 points on pain scale (epidural 3.87 vs control 4.95). This represents a substantial reduction in post-operative pain. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analysis reported, but the intervention appeared effective in the general gynecologic surgery population studied. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Some safety concerns with 4 epidural discontinuations and slightly higher complications (15 vs 12), but these did not prevent demonstration of efficacy.

failure_modes.evidence: While successful overall, 4 epidural discontinuations suggest the intervention may not work for all patients, though this represents a small minority
